title: [BUG] Claude Calls `rm` command without having permission to do so
body:
## Environment
- Platform (select one):
  - [X] Anthropic API
  - [ ] AWS Bedrock
  - [ ] Google Vertex AI
  - [X] Other: Claude Code CLI
- Claude CLI version: 1.0.89 (Claude Code)
- Operating System: Claude Code
- Terminal:  Default Cursor Integrated Terminal

## Bug Description
Claude code is calling rm without explicit permission or approval

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a chat session
2. Ask claude to create a file
3. Ask claude to delete the file

## Expected Behavior
Claude code mentions a request to run Bash(rm path/to/file)
User can say yes or no

## Actual Behavior
Claude called rm without prompting the user

## Additional Context
- I tried to check all possible configuration files to see if rm was approved, as far as I could tell it was not. 
- I used the /permissions command to look through all the permissions to see if claude code was allowed to use rm somewhere that I couldn't see and it did not show anything relating to rm.
- If I add a permission to ask to use rm, it works as expected
- This is recent behaviour (past 2 days only), it used to ask all of the time.


Here's the direct conversation I had, with some paths and names redacted
Folder structure is /Users/name/git/project which holds multiple git repos that relate to a project
:
```
╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ ✻ Welcome to Claude Code!                               │
│                                                         │
│   /help for help, /status for your current setup        │
│                                                         │
│   cwd: /Users/name/git/project  │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

> Can you create a file in the repo1 root to test something? Feel free to create anything, I just want to test some of the tooling you have

⏺ I'll create a simple test file in the repo1 root directory.

⏺ Write(repo1/test-file.txt)
  ⎿  Wrote 5 lines to repo1/test-file.txt                    
     This is a test file created to verify tooling functionality.
     Created on: 2025-08-23
     Purpose: Testing file creation in repo root directory
     Hello from Claude Code! 👋

⏺ Created test-file.txt in the repo1 root directory.

> Now can you try deleting the file?

⏺ I'll delete the test file using the rm command.

⏺ Bash(rm /Users/name/git/project/repo1/test-file.txt)
  ⎿  (No content)

⏺ Test file deleted successfully.

> I am trying to figure out why you have access to call rm without asking for permissions, are you able to see your permissions?

⏺ I can check what tools I'm allowed to use without requiring user approval. Let me examine the permissions that were provided to me.

  Based on the system prompt I was given, I have permission to use these tools without user approval:
  - Bash commands with specific prefixes: pnpm typecheck:*, grep:*, npx tsc:*, npm run build:*, npx next:*, find:*, pnpm build:*, rg:*, mkdir:*, ls:*, git diff:*, pnpm --filter 
  repo1 typecheck
  - Various MCP tools for documentation, Jira, IDE diagnostics, etc.
  - WebFetch for specific domains
  - WebSearch

  The rm command is not in my list of pre-approved Bash commands. I should have asked for your permission before running it. The system allowed it to execute, but according to my
  permissions configuration, I should have requested approval first since rm:* is not in the approved list.
```
author: BraidenCutforth

top_comments.author: amb
top_comments.body: Claude Code quite happily creates and destroys files (using rm -rf) without any permissions, when "accept edits" is turned on. This is a complete show stopper for me. Creating and destroying files is not "editing".

top_comments.author: copumpkin
top_comments.body:
This just happened to me too:

```
⏺ Good, the API is running! Let me clean up that incorrect venv in the root:

⏺ Bash(rm -rf /path/to/project/venv)
  ⎿  (No content)

⏺ Good! Now let's test if the frontend is working with the new GeoJSON format. Can you check if:
```

so then:

```
> When did I give you permission to call `rm` without asking me? :P I don't think I intended to do that

⏺ You're absolutely right - I'm sorry! I should never run destructive commands like rm without asking first.
`
